question: How should already-approved GPU experiments proceed after the user explicitly removed GPU-hour limits?
hypothesis: The existing validated scientific computation can complete under accounting-only GPU supervision; no runtime optimization or CPU feasibility experiment is needed.

sources.consequence: Keep the original local planner computation, full64 policy, tasks and all 3000 cases. Change only resource supervision and output location.

sources.sections: contextmanager generator, exception propagation and finally cleanup
sources.consequence: Replace only the GPU accounting context and remaining-time accessor; retain provenance, dedicated-device checks and terminal interval closure, and re-raise computation failures.
Install accounting functions before the original scientific module imports them, then execute its original CLI in one fresh child.
Track exact owned process identity, observe completion and retain reviewed bounded cleanup. No total-runtime deadline; a 30-minute lack of output progress is a stall trigger.
Keep exclusive ledger admission and closure; elapsed time remains recorded without enforcement of old global/stage allocations.

differences: Explicit user override of all previous global, stage and per-run GPU-hour budgets. Scientific scope, literature gates, serial GPU execution, model/data identity and numerical criteria remain. Initial implementation launches original object planning into fresh planning_full directories, preserving partial canonical outputs. Later approved GPU stages use this same authorization after their own unchanged scientific gates.
contrary_evidence: Removing time limits does not repair a hung GPU or establish scientific success. A missing output update is a liveness indication, not a measured scientific negative. Reusing old wrappers unchanged would still enforce superseded limits.

authorization.quote: Disregard the GPU hour limit, you've spent more time optimising down than it would've just taken to run it
authorization.scope: All GPU-hour limits in the active approved P25/P26 plan are removed; accounting continues.

Lock ledger and retain original scientific-ID inner interval plus C009 owned outer interval annotated U001. No absolute elapsed time limit. Hidden GPU,2threads,180seconds.
protocol.future: Adapt independent planning inspector to fresh paths/U001 operation metadata while the long GPU evaluation runs; scientific scoring remains unchanged. Downstream P26 and comparison consumers must explicitly bind the reviewed full outputs.

success: The user-authorized unlimited-time policy is actually used for progressing jobs, with exact input identity, recorded elapsed time and preserved failures; full scientific success remains separately measured.
stop: Refuse stale/missing parents, source drift, reused outputs, occupied GPU/open ledger. Stop only the exact owned child on confirmed progress timeout or operational exception; no total GPU-hour stop.
